clue.text: Planner has no latitude — he shouldn't throw a wobbly

indicators.note: having none of something means that item is missing from the word

parts.note: a plotter is someone who plans a scheme
L is the standard abbreviation for latitude

explanation.surface: A town planner forbidden to deviate, and warned not to lose his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: To throw a wobbly is to have a tantrum, but a potter throws pots on a wheel, and a wobbly one is a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A potter shapes clay by throwing it on a wheel, and a lopsided, wobbly pot is exactly what he must avoid.

clue.text: Plant scratching marks in semiconductor element

indicators.note: to scratch something is to strike it out, so the item is crossed off

parts.note: a metalloid element used in transistors
M stands for (Deutsch)marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A plant scratching marks into a semiconductor, as if in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The geranium is a common flowering garden plant, often grown in pots and window boxes.

clue.text: Cops almost trapping racehorse linked with cone section

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so one word goes within another
almost all of a word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: the police, plural like cops
the Arab is a breed of horse famed for racing

explanation.surface: Police nearly trapping a racehorse somehow connected to a coned-off section of road.
explanation.walkthrough: POLIC goes around ARAB. 'Cone section' suggests traffic cones, but it is geometry: slicing a cone gives conic sections.
explanation.definitionFit: A parabola is one of the conic sections, so parabolic describes something related to that curve.

clue.text: Marine personnel reported for sea trip

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound

parts.note: the crews of ships are their marine personnel

explanation.surface: Ships' staff are reported as signing up for a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a pleasure voyage at sea, a holiday trip aboard a ship.

clue.text: Not originally bound for Norway after drinking ale up

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Someone sailing for Norway after a few drinks, not bound by anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound for Norway' reads as a destination, but bound belongs to the definition and for is taken literally as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone freeborn was born free rather than into slavery or serfdom, so was never bound from birth.

clue.text: Relative is most confused when not having a rest

indicators.note: not having something means that portion is absent from the word

parts.note: least clear, i.e. most muddled
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member is at his most muddled when he has had no break.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a family relation, a parent's brother.

clue.text: Cut down tree?

parts.note: surface reading: a tree that has been felled
setter's reading: a tree kept tiny by pruning, cut down in size rather than felled

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' usually means felled; here it means reduced in size, as the Japanese art of miniature trees does by careful trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees, kept small by pruning roots and branches.

clue.text: Alfresco or outside exercises in a broadcast

indicators.note: one word placed outside the rest wraps around them

parts.note: taken as written
PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Choosing between an outdoor session and exercises in a televised broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like a synonym for the definition, but it is the wrapping instruction; exercises are PE, school physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco is Italian for 'in the fresh air', describing something done outdoors, such as dining.

clue.text: Dilapidated ruin, one abandoned on an upland

indicators.note: something abandoned has been left behind, so it drops out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
a down is an area of open rolling upland, as in the South Downs

explanation.surface: A crumbling ruin, a lonely abandoned house up on the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The downs are the chalk hills of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-down building has fallen into disrepair, which is what dilapidated means.

clue.text: North American sons all finally pay through the nose

parts.note: the standard abbreviation
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, its closing letter

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: An American family's sons all end up paying through the nose, i.e. overpaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay through the nose' is an idiom for being overcharged, but only the last three words are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak nasally is to sound as if through the nose, as with a cold.

clue.text: A crown regularly seen in this abroad

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken in turn

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A crown often spotted on royals overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled semicircular headpiece, a small crown worn by women on formal occasions.

clue.text: The output of brainstorming dreamers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split as two words: lists of ideas
second meaning: people who pursue lofty ideals

explanation.surface: Wondering whether brainstorming sessions just produce starry-eyed fantasists.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning needs the answer read as IDEA LISTS, what a brainstorming session writes up; the second takes it whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealists pursue perfect ideals over practical reality, so they are often dismissed as dreamers.

clue.text: Big beast runs wild — no heroics!

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so these letters go out of order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge animal charges about, and the onlooker is warned not to try anything brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs wild' reads as one phrase, but runs gives a single letter and wild works on what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is a massive horned African or Asian mammal, one of the largest land animals.

clue.text: Higher land might be cold without a coat

indicators.note: taking off a coat strips away the outer layer, so both edges go

parts.note: chilly is a word for cold

explanation.surface: Up on higher ground you will feel the cold if you go out with no coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first and last letters of CHILLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A hill is ground that rises above the surrounding land.

clue.text: Chic couple of humans (neither male) all stopping short for a dog

indicators.note: neither may keep the male, so the letter for male is taken from each
every word stops short, so each loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
two copies of human

explanation.surface: A fashionable pair, both women, with a pampered lapdog in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: Each HUMAN loses its M (male) and then its last letter; CHIC loses its last letter too.
explanation.definitionFit: The chihuahua is a tiny Mexican breed of dog, the smallest recognised breed.

clue.text: Any old people: Crazy, Cranky, Dotard and him

indicators.note: something crazy is deranged, so these letters are deranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of names for a motley bunch of oldies: Crazy, Cranky, Dotard and one more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old people' tempts toward dotards, but the definition is the idiom 'any old people', meaning anybody at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom, Dick and Harry is an idiom for ordinary people in general, anyone at all without distinction.

clue.text: Equatorial winds gripping island in storms

indicators.note: to grip something is to hold it in, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: the trade winds blow steadily towards the equator
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Tropical winds batter an island during a tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storms' looks like weather; it is a plural noun for outbursts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a storm of abuse or protest.

clue.text: Mink, sod and golf ground — animal, vegetable and mineral?

indicators.note: ground up means crushed and broken, so these letters are reduced and remade

parts.note: taken as written
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A list of a mink, some turf and a golf course, recalling the parlour game Animal, Vegetable or Mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the old classification of all things into the animal, vegetable and mineral kingdoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural history traditionally divided the world into three kingdoms: animal, vegetable and mineral.

clue.text: Deserter left to hang around island is sensible

indicators.note: to hang around a place is to surround it, so the pieces go either side

parts.note: a rat deserts a sinking ship
the standard abbreviation
Iona is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A sensible person would leave a deserter to hang around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Rats are said to desert a sinking ship, hence a rat is a deserter. Iona is a small island off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means based on reason and logic, so a rational person is sensible.

clue.text: Electric vehicle reversing in hurry

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: the abbreviation for electric
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An electric car backing out in a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to rush or move with great speed, a synonym for hurry.

clue.text: A lot of money put on one number here?

definitions.text: A lot of money put on one number here?

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the tail is lost

parts.note: cash is money
the Roman numeral for one
the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Is this where a gambler stakes a fortune on a single number?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the place: a gambling house where roulette players stake money on single numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a gambling venue where roulette lets players bet heavily on one number.

clue.text: Inside airplanes, the tickets for a number of Americans

indicators.note: inside means the answer sits within the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Discussing tickets for a group of Americans travelling by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a count but something that numbs; the American spelling drops the A of the British anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: An anesthetic numbs sensation, so it is a numbing agent; this spelling without the first A is American.

clue.text: Some nasty lessons, each connected with stigma

indicators.note: some of means only a part, so the answer is a run of letters within the phrase

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant lessons leave each pupil with a lasting stigma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stigma' suggests disgrace; here it is botany. In a flower, the style is the stalk joining the stigma to the ovary.
explanation.definitionFit: In a flower's pistil, each style is the slender stalk that carries the stigma, connecting it to the ovary.

clue.text: Conservative crank, for instance, is cunning

parts.note: the abbreviation for Conservative
a crank is an example of a lever

explanation.surface: A Tory eccentric proves to be wily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crank' suggests an oddball politician; it is the machine handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and cunning both describe someone quick-witted and ingenious.

clue.text: Breadmaker? Not half

indicators.note: not half means a half of the letters are missing from the word

parts.note: the clue word itself, ten letters

explanation.surface: Is a breadmaker any good? 'Not half!' comes the enthusiastic reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove five of the ten letters, READM, leaving the answer. 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker is the person whose trade is making bread.

clue.text: Wicked criminal lady pinching sparkler diamonds

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip tightly, so one word holds the others inside it
something criminal is bent, so these letters are bent into another order

parts.note: taken as written
a star sparkles
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A wicked female crook steals jewellery and diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged LADY grips STAR and D; 'pinching' suggests stealing, but it is the gripping instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Dastardly describes cowardly, mean-spirited wickedness, as of a villain.

clue.text: Song of a sailor's gaff

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
an ode is a lyric poem or song

explanation.surface: A sea shanty about a sailor's blunder, or his ship's spar.
explanation.walkthrough: A gaff is British slang for a home. 'Gaff' tempts as a blunder or a ship's spar, both apt for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a gaff is someone's house or flat, and an abode is a dwelling place.

clue.text: Ray and Mark well captivated by a muse dancing

indicators.note: something captivated is held captive, so it is placed inside
dancing letters move about and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
NB is nota bene, Latin for 'mark well'

explanation.surface: Two men, Ray and Mark, are entranced by a dancing muse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray and Mark' read like two names, but Ray is the definition and Mark goes with well.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a ray of sunlight.

clue.text: School's study holding a hundred back

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so the whole is read from the end
holding something means having it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: an étude is a musical study
A, then C, the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A school's study hall holds a hundred pupils at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: ETUDE holds AC as ET-AC-UDE, then the whole is read in reverse. 'School' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or train them, so the verb is a synonym of educate.
